events.content:
Done. Both routes render (200) and the production build passes TypeScript cleanly. Here's what I added:

**How it works** — this Next.js 16.4 canary ships React 19.3's stable `<ViewTransition>` component and a `transitionTypes` prop on `<Link>` (which feeds `React.addTransitionType` during navigation), so no experimental config flag was needed. A new `react-canary.d.ts` (`/// <reference types="react/canary" />`) pulls in the TypeScript definitions.

**Shared element morph** — the grid thumbnail in `app/ProductGrid.tsx` and the detail hero in `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` are each wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-image-${slug}`} share="product-image-morph">`. Because the two elements share a name across the navigation, React pairs them and the browser morphs position/size between thumbnail and hero; the CSS only tunes the timing (300ms).

**Directional page slides** — a new `app/template.tsx` remounts on every navigation, so the outgoing page runs its `exit` animation and the incoming page runs `enter`. The grid→detail links pass `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` (old page slides out left, new slides in from the right) and the back link passes `['nav-back']` (reversed). Untyped navigations like the browser back button fall back to a cross-fade.

**Suspense reveals** — both `<Suspense>` boundaries (grid skeleton and the detail info skeleton) are wrapped in `<ViewTransition update="suspense-reveal">`, so when streamed content replaces the skeleton it cross-fades over 250ms instead of popping.

**Reduced motion** — all the custom `::view-transition-*` animations in `app/globals.css` live inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and a `reduce` block sets `animation: none !important` on every view-transition pseudo-element (killing the default shared-element morph too, so updates apply instantly) and also stops the skeleton pulse.

One behavioral note: adding `template.tsx` means page state remounts on each navigation — that's what makes per-page enter/exit animations possible and has no visible effect in this app since pages hold no client state.
